subtitle: Ship agents, not demos: evaluation, guardrails, observability, cost control, fallbacks, and the human-review loop — the engineering between prototype and production
audience: Developers with working agent prototypes (LangGraph/CrewAI/RAG courses) facing real traffic, real money, and real incidents. All machinery (budgets, cascades, gates, samplers, redactors) runs as executable JS; production systems (tracing backends, model APIs, deploy pipelines) are represented by accurate patterns labeled for your stack.
outcomes: Run a demo-to-prod gap audit and prioritize by user harm, not engineering aesthetics
Budget latency (p50/p95/p99) across model calls, retrieval, and tools — with streaming and parallelism
Control cost with token accounting, model routing, caching layers, and batching
Design fallback cascades (retry → smaller model → cached → deterministic → human) with per-tier triggers
Gate deploys on gold evals with canary analysis and automatic rollback triggers
Enforce production guardrails: injection defense at scale, PII redaction, output filters, rate limits
Instrument traces, token/latency/cost dashboards, and alerts that page on behavior, not just errors
Operate the human-review loop: sampling, queue design, reviewer UX, feedback-into-gold flywheel
Respond to incidents with severity levels, runbooks, safe rollbacks, and blameless postmortems
Pass a launch review: ship checklist with evidence for a production support agent

assessment.q: Demo works; production timelines unknown. First artifact?
options: Demo-to-prod gap audit across eval/guardrails/obs/cost/fallbacks/review, prioritized by user harm
assessment.explain: Readiness is enumerated gaps priced by harm, not vibes. Audit first, build second (Ch.1).

assessment.q: p99 12s, p50 1.2s on an agent with 4 sequential model calls. Biggest lever?
options: Parallelize independent calls + stream partials + timeout the tail — p99 is sequential-chain + tail-latency dominated
assessment.explain: Tail latency compounds serially; parallelism collapses it, streaming hides it, timeouts bound it (Ch.2).

assessment.q: Token bill triples after launch. Ordered response?
options: Attribute spend (per-feature accounting) → cache repeats → route by difficulty → batch offline → right-size models per tier
assessment.explain: Cost control is measurement then levers in ROI order: accounting first, caching, routing, batching, rightsizing (Ch.3).

assessment.q: Primary model down during peak. Correct behavior?
options: Fallback cascade: retry → smaller/secondary model → cached/stale-with-label → deterministic safe mode → human queue — degraded, never dead
assessment.explain: Reliability tiers degrade gracefully with labeled staleness and human overflow. Dead is the only unacceptable tier (Ch.4).

assessment.q: Deploy passes unit tests, fails customers same day. Missing gate?
options: Gold conversation evals + canary with automatic rollback on metric breach — behavior gates, not just code gates
assessment.explain: Code gates don't cover behavior. Gold sets + canary analysis + auto-rollback gate production behavior (Ch.5).

assessment.q: Canary shows +2% errors, −1% latency, +5% cost. Ship?
options: No: error regression vetoes regardless of latency wins; cost needs its own gate — multi-metric gates with vetoes
assessment.explain: Canary gates compose like eval gates: vetoes (errors/safety) overrule improvements. Ship on all-green, never averages (Ch.5).

assessment.q: Attack traffic crafts tickets exfiltrating order data. Layers?
options: Input validation + scope rules + output filters (PII patterns) + rate limits + attempt logging + tool permission audits — defense in depth
assessment.explain: Production guardrails layer: validate in, scope decisions, filter out (PII), throttle, log, audit tools. No single layer holds (Ch.6).

assessment.q: Pager fires on 5xx rate only. What's missed?
options: Behavioral degradation: answer quality drops, grounding failures, cost spikes, latency tails — alert on behavior + economics, not just errors
assessment.explain: AI incidents are often silent (fluent wrongness). Alert on quality proxies, cost anomalies, and tail latency — errors are the last signal, not the first (Ch.7).

assessment.q: Review queue grows unboundedly. Fix shape?
options: Risk-based sampling (uncertain + high-stakes + random baseline) with queue SLAs and reviewer UX that makes decisions fast and loggable
assessment.explain: Review capacity is finite: sample by risk, SLA the queue, instrument reviewer UX. Feedback flows back into gold items (flywheel) (Ch.8).

assessment.q: Refund wrongly issued at 3am. First three actions?
options: Contain (disable path/feature-flag) → assess blast radius from audit logs → safe rollback; postmortem after, blameless, ending in gold items + guardrail
assessment.explain: Contain, assess, roll back — in that order, from runbooks. Postmortems produce prevention (gold items + gates), never blame (Ch.9).

assessment.q: Launch review: one artifact that matters most?
options: Evidence bundle: gold scores, gate results, canary plan, rollback procedure, audit completeness — proof, not prose
assessment.explain: Launch reviews approve evidence: measured behavior, enforced gates, reversible deploys, complete audit. Diagrams support; proof decides (Ch.10).

assessment.q: Caching answers across users with order data inside. Risk?
options: Cross-tenant leakage: cached personalized answers served to others — key caches by tenant + data class, never globally
assessment.explain: Cache keys must include tenant and data sensitivity. Global caches leak PII across users — isolation is a cache-design requirement (Ch.3/6).

project.title: The Launch Review
project.summary: Take the returns-resolution agent from prototype to launch-ready: gap audit, latency/cost budgets with measurements, fallback cascade, eval-gated deploy pipeline with canary + rollback, production guardrails, observability dashboards, review-queue design, incident runbooks — presented as an evidence bundle a launch board would approve.
requirements: Gap audit: prototype scored across eval/guardrails/obs/cost/fallbacks/review with harm-ranked priorities
Latency budget: p50/p95/p99 targets with per-call allocation, streaming plan, and timeout/parallelism design
Cost model: per-1k-task projection with caching/routing/batching levers quantified
Fallback cascade: 4+ tiers with triggers, labels, and human overflow; chaos-tested primary-down path
Deploy pipeline: gold gates + canary analysis + auto-rollback triggers + feature-flag kill switches
Guardrails: injection/PII/rate-limit/output-filter layers with attack gold items
Observability: trace schema, dashboard list (latency/cost/quality), alert rules with behavioral signals
Review ops: sampling policy, queue SLAs, reviewer UX, feedback-to-gold flywheel
Incident kit: severity levels, two runbooks (wrong-refund, data-leak suspicion), rollback procedure
technical: All machinery (budgets, cascades, gates, samplers, redactors) in runnable JS with asserted behaviors
Gold sets versioned; canary analysis scripted with veto logic
Audit completeness: every money path logged with consumer/args/verdict/outcome
Numbers reproducible: budgets from measurements, costs from projections, gates from gold runs
project.architecture: Five sections: (1) Gap audit with harm ranking; (2) Budgets — latency/cost models with measurements; (3) Safety — fallbacks, guardrails, gates, canary, rollback; (4) Operations — observability, review ops, incident kit; (5) Launch evidence — scores, gate results, residual risks with owners and dates.
steps: Audit the prototype; rank gaps by user harm
Measure latency/cost baselines; write budgets with headroom
Write gold gates + canary analysis + rollback triggers
Add guardrails, observability, review ops, incident kit in that order
Assemble the evidence bundle; red-team it (attack gold) before submitting
evaluation: Every gap has an owner, a fix, and a verification method
Budgets derived from measurements with stated headroom; fallbacks chaos-proven
Gates block on violations (demonstrated with a failing case), canary vetoes honored
Guardrails layered with attack gold passing; audit complete per money path
Residual risks named with owners and dates — no silent hope
stretch: Load-test to 10x expected traffic and report the breaking tier with graphs
Add semantic caching with tenant-isolated keys and measure hit-rate + savings
Run a game-day: simulated wrong-refund incident end to end with timed runbook

interviewQs.a: Everything around the model: gold evals with gates, guardrails (injection/PII/rate limits), observability (traces, cost, quality alerts), latency budgets with streaming/parallelism, cost controls (caching, routing), fallback cascades, canary deploys with rollback, human review ops, and incident runbooks. The model call is 10% of production; the other 90% is what this course covers — audited in a gap analysis priced by user harm.

interviewQs.q: p99 is 10x p50 on your agent. Diagnose and fix.
interviewQs.a: Diagnose per-call timing distributions: serial model calls stack tails, retrieval outliers, tool timeouts without bounds. Fix in order: parallelize independent calls, stream partials to hide latency, bound every call with timeouts, cache repeats, route easy cases to smaller models. Measure p50/p95/p99 per tier after each change — tails move only when measured, and averages hide them by definition.

interviewQs.q: How do you gate AI deploys differently from code deploys?
interviewQs.a: Code gates (tests, types) plus behavior gates: gold conversation sets with per-segment no-regression rules, canary analysis on error/quality/cost metrics with vetoes, automatic rollback triggers, and feature flags for instant kills. Behavior drifts silently where code breaks loudly — gates must measure outcomes (hit-rate, faithfulness, violation counts), not just passage of tests.

interviewQs.q: Design fallbacks for a support agent whose model API dies at peak.
interviewQs.a: Cascade: bounded retry → secondary/smaller model → cached/stale-labeled answers → deterministic safe mode (status + human queue) — degraded tiers, never dead. Each tier labeled honestly to users; overflow routes to humans with context attached. Chaos-test the primary-down path quarterly; fallbacks untested are wishes, and wishes fail at peak.

interviewQs.q: Support agent with order data: caching strategy without leaking PII?
interviewQs.a: Key caches by (tenant, data-class, query-signature): per-user personalization never shares keys across tenants; public policy answers share broadly with version tags. Never cache across trust boundaries; TTL by freshness class (prices short, policies long); log cache hits for audit. Global caches on personalized data are cross-tenant leaks with extra steps.

interviewQs.q: Wrong refund issued at 3am. Walk me through it.
interviewQs.a: Contain first (feature-flag the refund path off — seconds), assess blast radius from audit logs (who/what amounts), roll back deploy if code-caused or revoke scope if abuse, then blameless postmortem producing gold items (the exact attack/edge), a gate (amount validation), and an owner with a date. Page on behavioral signals so 3am becomes 3pm prevention next time.
